prompt: Implement the batch operations and order-preserving resizing in this C99 integer FIFO. Keep the public API in ring.h and the existing CLI. A non-NULL ring handle is required for every operation. ring_create accepts any capacity including zero; capacities greater than SIZE_MAX / sizeof(int), or allocation failures, return NULL. size and capacity report the current counts. ring_push appends up to min(n, capacity-size) integers and returns that count; NULL input with n>0 returns zero without changing the ring. ring_pop removes up to min(n,size) integers in FIFO order, writes them to output when output is non-NULL, and discards them otherwise. Both operations accept n=0 with NULL buffers and must work across wraparound and with n=SIZE_MAX without arithmetic overflow. Input/output arrays must have room for the transferred integers. ring_resize returns 0 on success or -1 on failure; it preserves all queued values in FIFO order, rejects capacities below size or above SIZE_MAX/sizeof(int), and leaves the ring unchanged on failure. Resizing to the current capacity succeeds, shrinking to exactly size succeeds, and an empty ring may resize to zero and grow again. Operations on a zero-capacity ring transfer zero. ring_destroy accepts NULL. Avoid leaks, invalid accesses, and undefined behavior. No external dependencies. Run make test; make builds the ring_demo CLI, which prints all integer arguments in FIFO order separated by spaces followed by a newline (including an empty line with no arguments).
